# RSObject

`RSObject` is the root of RObjC object classes. Declare an application class
with `RSObjectClass()`, then create instances with its `$new()` method. An
instance inherits methods for class identity, protocol conformance, method
lookup, descriptions, equality, and hashing.

## Define and initialize a subclass

The class factory attaches identity metadata before instances are created.
When overriding `initialize()`, call `super$initialize()` so the instance gets
its R class attributes. Subclass state can live in R6 private fields.

```{r}
library(robjc)

Item <- RSObjectClass(
  "ObjectGuideItem",
  public = list(
    initialize = function(name) {
      super$initialize()
      private$.name <- name
      invisible(self)
    },
    name = function() private$.name
  ),
  private = list(.name = NULL),
  version = "1.0.0"
)
first <- Item$new("first")
second <- Item$new("first")
stopifnot(identical(first$name(), "first"))
```

## Inspect class relationships

`class()` returns the RObjC class generator. `isMemberOf()` tests exact class
identity, whereas `isKindOf()` also accepts ancestors. `superClass()` returns
the immediate parent generator. Read the class version from the generator's
`robjc_isa$version`. Class relationship checks use generator identity rather
than comparing class-name strings.

```{r}
stopifnot(identical(first$class(), Item))
stopifnot(first$isMemberOf(Item))
stopifnot(!first$isMemberOf(RSObject))
stopifnot(first$isKindOf(RSObject))
stopifnot(identical(first$superClass(), RSObject))
stopifnot(identical(first$class()$robjc_isa$version, "1.0.0"))
```

`inheritClassesAsList()` exposes the ancestry as generators. Use
`respondsTo("name")` to check whether an instance has a callable method.
`conformsTo(protocol)` reports protocol relationships declared on its class or
an ancestor; it does not inspect method bodies.

```{r}
stopifnot(first$respondsTo("name"))
stopifnot(!first$respondsTo("missingMethod"))
stopifnot(first$conformsTo(RSCopying))
```

## Identity, presentation, and copying

The base `isEqual()` compares object references: two objects with the same
fields are still distinct. The base `hash()` derives an integer from the
object's pointer, so subclasses that define value equality should also define
a compatible value hash. A custom `hash()` must return one non-missing integer:
pass its final computed value to `normalize_hash()` before returning it. This
maps the `NA_integer_` bit pattern to `0L`; equal objects must still have the
same hash. `objectID()` returns a pointer string.

`description()` gives a compact class-and-pointer label; `print()` outputs that
label, while `debugDescription()` includes public fields. The default `copy()`
returns the same instance. A mutable subclass should override `copy()` if it
needs an independent copy.

```{r}
stopifnot(first$isEqual(first))
stopifnot(!first$isEqual(second))
stopifnot(identical(first$copy(), first))
stopifnot(is.character(first$description()))
stopifnot(is.character(first$objectID()))
```

## Equality in a dictionary

`RSDictionary` illustrates why `hash()` and `isEqual()` must agree. Its native
table uses a key's `hash()` to find a bucket and `isEqual()` to distinguish
keys within that bucket. Two separate `RSString` objects with the same text
are equal by value and have the same hash, so either can retrieve an entry.

```{r}
stored_key <- RSString_withValue("id")
lookup_key <- RSString_withValue("id")
dictionary <- RSDictionary$new(
  keys = list(stored_key),
  values = list(RSString_withValue("one"))
)
stopifnot(!identical(stored_key, lookup_key))
stopifnot(stored_key$isEqual(lookup_key))
stopifnot(identical(stored_key$hash(), lookup_key$hash()))
stopifnot(identical(dictionary$objectForKey(lookup_key)$value(), "one"))
```

The required rule for a key class is: if `a$isEqual(b)` is `TRUE`, then
`a$hash()` and `b$hash()` must be identical. Equal hashes do **not** prove
equality. In particular, `RSDictionary$hash()` combines only its keys, so
changing a value can leave the dictionary hash unchanged even though the
dictionaries are unequal:

```{r}
other_dictionary <- RSDictionary$new(
  keys = list(lookup_key),
  values = list(RSString_withValue("two"))
)
stopifnot(identical(dictionary$hash(), other_dictionary$hash()))
stopifnot(!dictionary$isEqual(other_dictionary))
```

Dictionary insertion calls a key's `copy()`; the stored key must keep its
equality and hash state stable afterward. A mutable key class should provide
an appropriate copy and avoid changing fields used by `hash()` or `isEqual()`
while a key is stored. For copy behavior and missing keys, see
`vignette("robjc_dictionary", package = "robjc")`.

For protocol declarations and inherited requirements, see
`vignette("robjc_protocol", package = "robjc")`. For the class factory
arguments, see `vignette("robjc_class_factories", package = "robjc")`.
